title: Spring greens slaw on toast with cottage cheese

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is plain whole food or simple staples; tahini and cottage cheese are on the store cupboard list and nothing is a jarred sauce or packet mix.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including tahini and cottage cheese, is an everyday item at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: A knife, grater, bowl, whisk, small pan and an ordinary toaster or grill are all it needs, and the technique is simple.

works.reason: Finely shredded and salted spring greens with carrot and radish make a good raw slaw, and the tahini dressing loosened with lemon and water is well balanced for four slices of toast.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is realistic for shredding greens, grating two carrots, slicing radishes and spring onions, whisking the dressing and toasting, and three minutes suits toasting the seeds.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A fresh raw slaw suits late May, and the spring greens are the bulk and point of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps read as clear, plain British English instructions with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholemeal toast with cottage cheese and a generous vegetable slaw is a satisfying, balanced snack a family would make again.
